paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think Paul is teaching in this passage: the Christian life is flee and pursue, with a fight in the middle. Paul tells Timothy to flee the love of money (1 Timothy 6:10-11), and then he hands him a list to chase: righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance and gentleness. He says, "Fight the good fight of the faith." (1 Timothy 6:12) I think that means you don't drift into a faithful life, you run toward one on purpose, and I'm out here swinging with nothing but a mustache.

Now the money part. Paul doesn't say money is the enemy, and he doesn't say the rich should feel bad. He says not to put hope in "the uncertainty of wealth, but in God, who richly provides all things for us to enjoy." (1 Timothy 6:17) Then he says to be "rich in good works," and to be "generous and ready to share," (1 Timothy 6:18) because that is how they take hold of "that which is truly life." (1 Timothy 6:19) So your hope goes in God, not in the pile, and that leaves your hands open to give.

And all of it sits under one big picture. Timothy is to keep the commandment "until the appearance of our Lord Jesus Christ," which God "will bring about in His own time." (1 Timothy 6:14-15) That's why I keep my ovens ready, and it's why Paul tells Timothy to guard what he was given and stay away from empty chatter (1 Timothy 6:20). So, baker, hold on to Jesus, hold your money loosely, and keep your oven ready. You don't have to do any of it on your own strength, because Paul closes with "Grace be with you all." (1 Timothy 6:21)
